introHeading: The 3D slider booth for Manhattan's stages and show floors
introParas: Manhattan venues run on somebody else's clock — a loading dock reservation, a freight elevator window, a building engineer who signs off at six. The 3D slider adds one more variable to that conversation: the motorized track needs roughly 12ft of clear width at normal ceiling height, more than our other booths ask for, so we confirm the fit against your floor plan before you book rather than discovering a squeeze on the day. We send the certificate of insurance your venue needs ahead of time as part of that same process.

The payoff is a format most Manhattan guests haven't seen before. A camera glides along the track past your guests mid-pose, capturing the moment from multiple angles in one take — the stitched result has genuine depth, and people replay it on the spot to watch the effect again. That novelty is exactly why it gets booked for SoHo product launches and Financial District conferences: the unusual clip earns the post on its own, and a branded overlay rides along on every capture. Motion effects and a backdrop chosen in advance let it match a corporate stage as easily as a wedding reception in a Tribeca loft.

Every rental includes a trained attendant, unlimited sessions and instant delivery by text, email or QR code, with an online gallery afterward. Manhattan is a standard service area — travel is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book, never added later — and we're out across Midtown, Chelsea, the Financial District and the rest of the borough most weekends.

faqs.q: Will the 3D slider fit in a smaller Manhattan venue or gallery space?
faqs.a: It needs more room than our other booths — roughly 12ft of clear width at normal ceiling height for the track to glide along. Some gallery spaces and tighter hotel event rooms can't accommodate that; send us your floor plan and we'll confirm the fit before you book, and suggest an alternative booth if the slider won't work.

faqs.q: Do you provide a COI for Manhattan buildings that require one?
faqs.a: Yes, as standard practice. Most Manhattan buildings ask for a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured before approving load-in — send us their contact information and we'll get it to them ahead of your date.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee for the 3D slider in Manhattan?
faqs.a: Manhattan is a standard service area — any travel fee is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book, never added to the invoice afterward.

faqs.q: Can the slider be branded for a corporate product launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Every capture can carry a branded overlay — your logo, campaign frame or event graphics — and the backdrop is chosen with you in advance, so the whole experience matches your activation rather than sitting apart from it.

faqs.q: How much space does the 3D slider need?
faqs.a: Roughly 12ft across at normal ceiling height, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet. It's the widest footprint of our open-air booths, which is why we confirm the fit before you book.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental, coaching guests through each slide and handling setup and pack-down.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you meet an early building sign-off deadline?
faqs.a: We arrive a full hour before your scheduled start so the track, camera and lighting are tested and ready. If your building requires an earlier load-in than that, we can typically accommodate it — idle time before your booked hour runs at $150 per hour.

faqs.q: How much liability insurance do you carry?
faqs.a: We carry a $3 million liability insurance policy. If your venue's management office needs the certificate before confirming your booking, let us know and we'll send it promptly.
